conventions.convention: KL is directed from p to q; zero p-coordinate terms are omitted, and positive p mass at a zero q coordinate gives +∞. The objective is expected reward minus β times this KL, with β>0.
Bradley–Terry comparisons concern distinct responses and use σ(r(a)−r(b)) for the probability that a is preferred to b; each response set has at least two elements.
The Gibbs optimum assumes finite nonempty response space, full-support reference, finite real rewards and β>0; policies being optimized may have zero coordinates.
DPO records are ordered winner/loser triples; the policy family is positive and C1 on an open parameter domain, and gradients are Euclidean column vectors.

The update schedule starts at t=0 and has T≥0 attempts. Mini-batches are nonempty ordered lists with repetitions allowed. Exact terminating primitive evaluators and parameter-membership oracle are supplied; reverse AD uses unique strict branches. The max/absolute-value loss implementation is not differentiated.

load_bearing.statement: For finite nonempty Y, full-support probability vector q, real reward r and β>0, Z=Σ_y q_y exp(r(y)/β) is finite and positive and p*_y=q_y exp(r(y)/β)/Z is a full-support probability vector. F(p*)=β log Z and F(p*)−F(p)=β D(p||p*)≥0 for every probability vector p, with equality exactly when p=p*.

Under finite response sets of size at least two, positive reference probabilities, real rewards and β>0, reward differences equal β times differences of Gibbs-policy/reference log ratios. Conversely every full-support policy is the unique Gibbs policy for reward β log(π/q), with prompt-only offsets preserving policy and comparisons. For a nonempty finite ordered winner/loser dataset and positive C1 policy family on an open domain, the average loss log(1+exp(−u_i)) is the Bradley–Terry negative log likelihood and has gradient −(β/n)Σ_i σ(−u_i)(∇log π(w_i|x_i)−∇log π(l_i|x_i)).

For every input of the finite-budget DPO procedure under its supplied exact evaluator and membership-oracle model, prescribed loss evaluations are finite, successful reverse sweeps give the exact mini-batch gradient, and the stored pair remains the most recently accepted parameter in Θ together with its full-data loss. The procedure terminates after at most T attempted updates with the specified status. For M=Σ_t m_t, work excluding membership is O(C[n(T+1)+M+T+1]) for finite graph-dependent C≥d+1; there are at most T membership calls, whose actual finite costs are added separately.

For probability vectors p,q on finite nonempty Y, D(p||q) is the sum of p_y log(p_y/q_y) over positive p coordinates when p is supported on q, and +∞ otherwise. For real reward r and β>0, maximize F(p)=Σ_y p_y r(y)−β D(p||q) over all probability vectors p.
